jobs.title: Director of Development
jobs.description:
**About Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay**

Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to build decent, affordable homes and provide home ownership opportunities to qualified families who live and work in Santa Cruz Counties. Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is an independent, locally operated and funded affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development is responsible for leading Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's fundraising, donor engagement, and development operations. This role secures philanthropic revenue, cultivates donor relationships, oversees fundraising campaigns, and implements strategic development initiatives that advance the organization's mission.

The position requires strong relationship-building skills, strategic thinking, and a commitment to driving sustainable revenue growth in support of Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay's mission.

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities: Fundraising & Revenue Development**

* Plan, implement, and manage annual fundraising strategies to meet organizational revenue goals
* Supervise, coach, and mentor the Fundraising and Development Manager and foster a collaborative culture or philanthropy across staff, volunteers, and the Board, so that everyone in the organization sees a role in resource development.
* Participate in all aspects of the gift cycle from initiating contacts through stewardship.
* Meet specific annual fundraising goals and contact metrics set by the Chief Executive Officer.
* Lead donor cultivations, solicitation, and stewardship efforts, including individual giving, major donors, and monthly donor programs.
* Develop and execute online fundraising initiatives and seasonal appeals.

**Donor & Community Engagement**

* Steward donors through personalized communication, meetings, and engagement activities.
* Oversee donor recognition initiatives and maintain accurate records in the organization's donor database (Bloomerang).
* Plan and coordinate fundraising events, community fundraising, and donor appreciation events.
* Collaborate with program staff to develop compelling proposals, reports, and presentations for donors
* Support organization-wide events, outreach efforts, and public communications as needed.

**Administrative & Organizational Support**

* Oversee donor recognition initiatives and maintain accurate records in the organization's donor database (CRMs).
* Analyze donor data to tailor fundraising approaches.
* Participate in the creation of the annual development plan and metrics for corporate and foundation relations and major gifts.
* Manage the annual schedule of grant deadlines. Work in partnership with subject matter experts and Grant Writer to complete and submit grant applications.
* Support organization-wide events, outreach efforts, and public communications as needed.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Education and Experience: Minimum 3 years experience in nonprofit fundraising, development, donor relations, or similar role.
* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, communications, marketing, or related field; equivalent experience considered.
* Reliable transportation and ability to work on site weekly at office and as needed at partner locations throughout Santa Cruz and Monterey Counties.

**Required Skills**

* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to effectively engage and cultivate relationships with diverse stakeholders.
* Demonstrates high level professionalism in all written and verbal communications, appearance, and interactions.
* Demonstrated success in meeting or exceeding fundraising goals.
* Skilled in creating powerful, compelling written and oral communications for fundraising efforts through storytelling.
* Strong project management and organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Proficiency with Bloomerang/CRM, Microsoft Office, and marketing tools such as Canva.
* Ability to work independently toward big picture goals and effectively collaborate with others.

*This job description is intended to convey information essential to understanding the scope of the position and is not exhaustive. Responsibilities and duties may change as the needs of the organization evolve.*

**Physical Demands**

The Director of Development will experience frequent sitting and repetitive motion.

**Working Conditions**

Must be able to work occasional evenings and weekends. Ability to lift 30 pounds. This position requires both off-site and in-person work at a desk and at community events and partnership sites. Some occasional outdoor work may be required for this position.

**Benefits**

Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay offers medical, dental, vision, and life insurance benefits, along with paid time off.

**How to Apply**

Submit resume and cover letter to: admin@habitatmontereybay.org. Attention: Maria Lopez.

*Habitat for Humanity Monterey Bay is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, or disability.*

Pay: $110,000.00 - $130,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
New Destiny’s mission is to end the cycle of domestic violence and homelessness for low-income families and individuals by developing and connecting them to safe, permanent, affordable housing and services. To achieve its mission, New Destiny builds and manages housing with on-site services; offers innovative programs that assist survivors in finding and retaining affordable housing; and works to expand access to permanent housing resources for survivors. New Destiny is the largest provider of supportive housing for domestic violence survivors in New York and is a leading advocate in the effort to obtain the resources needed to end family homelessness in New York City.

**General Description**

New Destiny is seeking to hire a full-time Program Director to provide regular on-site services at two supportive housing locations in The Bronx. This role ensures consistent, trauma-informed practice in case management, crisis intervention, and community organizing, while supervising staff and coordinating with external partners. This is a full-time position

requiring one late night a week (e.g., 11:00 am to 7:00 pm). The Program Director will report directly to the Regional Director.

**Responsibilities**

**Tenant Engagement and Community Organizing:**

* Build a team to actively engage tenants to participate in program services and activities.

* Foster tenant interaction and build community within the building. In doing so, develop and implement

workshops that reflect the interests of tenants.

* Work collaboratively with colleagues to plan enriching activities for children and adults.

* Maintain transparency with tenants regarding expectations, requirements and provide support as needed.

* Build relationships with local community organizations, legal aid, healthcare providers, employment services, etc. in order to bring programming and referral sources to the tenants.

**Supervision of Case Management Services:**

* Supervise case managers at both sites, provide guidance on survivor-centered trauma-informed care.

* Split time between both sites to supervise operations, maintain visibility with staff and residents, and ensure program consistency.

* Review case files, service plans, and housing stability goals. Ensure all data entry for team is timely and accurate.

* Collaborate with Family Support Program staff at other sites to learn/share best practices and with community partners.

* Ensure team is working to mitigate rental arrears and collaborate with New Destiny’s Property Management team.

* Provide leadership, coaching, performance evaluations, staff education, and ongoing staff support.

* Oversee escalated incidents, including threats to safety and mental health crises.

**Administrative Duties:**

* Strong administrative abilities and attention to detail. Ability to adjust to the diverse needs of tenants.

* Ensure outcomes are met for funders and internal goals.

* Conduct ongoing internal monitoring and data analysis.

* Manage internal reporting for Regional Director, VP of Supportive Housing, CEO, and OTDA reporting.

* Manage and maintain relationship with property management department, mental health team and financial coaches.

**Requirements**

* Master's degree preferred in psychology, social work, or related field, bachelor’s degree required.

* A minimum of 5 years' work experience in a client-facing, nonprofit organization.

* A minimum of 3-5 years of supervisory experience in a social service setting.

* Familiarity working with survivors of domestic violence and/or homelessness.

* Must be responsible, flexible, a self-starter, able to work independently and respond appropriately to crises.

* Excellent communication and organizational skills.

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, teams, share point and power point.

* Experience with trauma-informed care.

**Preferred candidates will have:**

* Strong preference for Spanish fluency.

* Comprehensive knowledge of benefits, entitlements and services offered in NYC

**How to Apply**

Please visit https://newdestinyhousing.org/about-us/jobs-and-internships/ to apply for this position.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
**Adult Day Care Program Director**

**Richmond Adult Day Care** is seeking a **Program Director** for our Adult Day Care in Staten Island, New York. The Ideal candidate will have a background in ADC and be extremely organized.

**Must have Managerial Experience**

**Competitive Compensation & comprehensive benefits package.**

**DUTIES:**

* Perform/direct all marketing/outreach activities related to diversifying the registrant base in order to increase/maintain program census in accordance with CHC strategic plan.
* Plan, develop, organize, and implement all activities and services provided by the program.
* Ensure that established guidelines, regulations, and fiscal restraints are observed.
* Develop & maintain administrative plans and procedures.
* Coordinate admission data with RN and Social Worker.
* Evaluate for eligibility for acceptance into the program.
* Oversight of all staff, students & volunteers, including hiring, training, managing, evaluating, and terminating.
* Ensures compliance with licensing regulations.
* Prepares and conducts information, outreach, education & advocacy programs related to the services offered.
* Partake in community & professional meetings/seminars, including the ADC Council.
* Prepare monthly reports including census, summary of daily operations, etc.

**REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor's degree in the healthcare field is a plus.
* Candidates with an Adult Day Care background are preferred.
* Should have prior management experience.
* Strong leadership & interpersonal skills.
* Must be well organized and able to lead team development.
* Excellent oral/written communication skills.

jobs.title: Deputy Director - Tourism & Events
jobs.description:
**Introduction**
----------------

The Deputy Director of Tourism & Events serves as a key operational leader, providing day-to-day management of the department and oversight of the City’s major tourism and cultural contracts. Reporting directly to the Senior Director, this role is responsible for ensuring consistent execution, performance accountability, and alignment with the City’s strategic priorities. This position is central to the effective administration of Scottsdale’s tourism and events portfolio. The Deputy Director oversees the City’s relationships with its contracted partners, including Experience Scottsdale and Scottsdale Arts, ensuring contractual obligations are met, performance is monitored, and issues are identified and addressed proactively.
  
While the Senior Director serves as the City’s primary strategic and external-facing leader, the Deputy Director ensures that departmental operations, contract administration, and team performance are executed with consistency, discipline, and attention to detail. This role requires a highly organized and thoughtful professional who can translate policy and agreements into day-to-day operations, manage competing priorities, and support a high-performing, accountable team environment.

**NOTE: Please submit a cover letter describing your interest in the Deputy Director of Tourism & Events position and explaining how your professional experience has prepared you to succeed in this role.**

*Anticipated starting salary for this position may be up to mid-point depending on candidate’s experience and internal equity. The full salary range is listed above and mid-point for this position is $147,950.40 annually.*

**Please note:** **Be sure to check your email junk/spam folders regularly for possible notifications and/or self-schedule interview invitations from Governmentjobs.**

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Urban Planning, Economic Development or related field from an accredited educational institution.
* Seven years of progressively responsible managerial experience in municipal government or a comparably complex public-sector organization, including responsibility for supervising professional staff, administering programs and contracts, and coordinating work across organizational functions.
* Any equivalent combination of education and/or job-related experience that meets the minimum qualifications may be substituted.
* Preferred: experience in tourism, destination management, special events, economic development, marketing, cultural affairs or closely related field.
* Preferred: Participation in relevant professional associations, including leadership roles.

**Licensing, Certifications and Other Requirements**
  

* Must possess, at time of application, and maintain a valid, unrestricted driver's license with no major citations within the past 36 months prior to the start date. The Arizona Motor Vehicle Department requires that out-of-state driver's licenses must be surrendered within 10 days of relocating to the State of Arizona. **Note**: Graduated Driver’s Licenses are considered restricted.
* Every person employed by the City of Scottsdale shall reside in the State of Arizona during active employment by the city, regardless of whether the employee is approved for remote work.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

***To view the job description and list of Essential Functions,*** ***click here******.***

**Work Environment/Physical Demands**
-------------------------------------

***To view the Work Environment/Physical Demands,*** ***c******lick here******.***
  
  
**Selection Process:**
  
The application and supplemental questions are an integral part of the selection process and must be completed in full in order for you to be considered as a candidate. Please complete each section and answer all questions as thoroughly as possible.**DO NOT state “See Resume” in lieu of answering.** Unanswered questions, incomplete responses, omissions, or partial information may result in disqualification from the selection process.
  
  
Applicants whose education, training and experience most closely meet the needs of the position may be invited to participate in a selection process that may include a panel interview. Successful candidates will receive a post-offer, pre-employment background screening that may include:

* Fingerprinting search of the national FBI Database
* Criminal Background screening
  

  

**The City of Scottsdale reserves the right to change this process at any time, potentially without advance notice.**

**PLEASE NOTE:** Years of experience are based on a work schedule of 2,080 hours per year for full-time positions and 1,040 hours per year for part-time positions, and while work experience may substitute for education on a year-for-year basis, depending upon the job classification, education may not be substituted for work experience.

**EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY:** It is the policy of the city to provide employment opportunities to all persons based solely on ability, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability.

When advised, reasonable accommodations will be made in order for an "otherwise qualified applicant" with a disability to participate in any phase of the recruitment process. Please contact Human Resources to request an accommodation. Persons with a disability may request a reasonable accommodation by contacting HR at (480) 312-2491. Requests should be made 24 hours in advance or as early as possible to allow time to arrange the accommodation. For TTY users, the Arizona Relay Service (1-800-367-8939) may contact HR at (480) 312-2491.
